The browser sends only an id-only history, never the learner's free text.
alternatives: Keep only the scoring planner; let the model choose without validation; send the learner's explanations to the planner.
reason: The scoring planner is a pre-fixed rule. A model suggestion is allowed to replace it, but only inside a validator, and its source is always visible.
owner: TEAM via AI-assisted build (individual not recorded)
risk: A model may suggest a pedagogically poor order. The screen calls it a suggestion, not a validated assessment. Two model calls per re-check double the latency and the rate-limit use.
reopen_trigger: A teacher reviews real suggestions and finds them unhelpful, or latency is unacceptable on the demo network.
next_action: PATHASETU_MODEL_PLANNING=off switches the model planner off and keeps the labelled built-in planner.

decision: Retry limits and timings, and the model time budgets, come from the environment (PATHASETU_RETRY_MAX_ATTEMPTS, _BASE_DELAY_MS, _FACTOR, _MAX_DELAY_MS, PATHASETU_MODEL_TIMEOUT_MS, _DEADLINE_MS). The documented defaults (5 attempts, 5 s base, factor 2, 60 s cap, 20 s per provider, 45 s per chain) apply only when a variable is unset; a set but invalid value stops startup. The server reports the values in /api/health and the browser uses them, including the re-check timeout.
alternatives: Constants in the browser; a settings screen for learners.
reason: The retry numbers were constants in the shipped page. Configuration by the operator, validated at startup, removes the constants without adding a learner-facing setting.
owner: TEAM via AI-assisted build (individual not recorded)
risk: The default numbers are still numbers someone chose; they are defaults, not evidence-based values. A very long re-check timeout holds the queue entry in flight.

decision: A draft-question generator (npm run generate:drafts) asks the configured chain for new questions on a concept already in the pack. Output is written outside content/, public/, src/ and scripts/, every item is forced to UNREVIEWED_DRAFT with no reviewer, carries provenance (provider, model, time, reviewRequired), and is validated structurally; nothing is loaded by the app.
alternatives: Let the model add questions straight to the pack; skip the structural validation.
reason: Generated science questions can be wrong or ambiguous. The only safe path is a draft file a qualified teacher reviews before anything is copied by hand.
owner: TEAM via AI-assisted build (individual not recorded)
risk: Structural validity is not scientific correctness. No generated item has been seen by a teacher; no real model produced one here.
reopen_trigger: A teacher agrees to review generated drafts.

decision: A hosted provider (Gemini, Groq, or an Ollama URL that is not loopback) requires a strong demo access code at startup, and preflight requires PATHASETU_PROVIDER_DATA_CONTROLS_ACK=true. API keys travel only in request headers, never in a URL, body, log or error. Failed provider calls expose stable codes only, never an upstream body. Test, capture and preflight servers blank PATHASETU_MODEL_PROVIDERS so a shell variable cannot send test data to a model.
alternatives: Open endpoint for local use only; pass the key in the URL.
reason: The existing Groq rules were extended to every hosted provider so the new providers are no weaker than the old one.
owner: TEAM via AI-assisted build (individual not recorded)
risk: This is lightweight demo protection, not production authentication. Learner text goes to Google or Groq when those are configured.
reopen_trigger: Any plan to use real children's responses.
next_action: Review each provider's data controls before the first hosted run.

decision: Gemini is called with responseMimeType application/json and the JSON Schema is placed in the system instruction, not in a schema field, because the Gemini documentation fetched during research did not let the build confirm a responseSchema or responseJsonSchema field for generateContent. Every model name must be set explicitly.
alternatives: Send responseSchema; default to a model name.
reason: Avoiding an unconfirmed field is safer than guessing one. A default model name would be a pre-fixed choice that goes out of date.

decision: A saved record with a missing answers, queue or trace array was previously returned unrepaired and reported as having no repairs, which would crash the page later. decision: What is still fixed, stated plainly: the list of allowed misconceptions for each question (content, set by the pack), the 0.65 confidence floor in the validator, the option-linked rule that gives the very first offline feedback in the browser (before any model is reachable), the built-in planner used as the labelled fallback, and the default retry and time numbers. The request that nothing be hard-coded is therefore met for the online diagnosis, the next-question choice, the retry settings and question drafting, and not met for the offline first feedback or the safety validator.
alternatives: Remove the offline rule (leaves a learner offline with no feedback); make the confidence floor configurable.
reason: A browser with no network cannot call a model, and a validator that a model could loosen would no longer be a guard.
